summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic pancreatitis and a history of recent candidemia from a central line was admitted with an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control using IV Dilaudid, a PCA pump, and transition to oral opioids. A PICC line was placed on 2170-09-06 to initiate TPN due to ongoing malnutrition and inability to eat. Right-sided back pain developed but resolved spontaneously with no evidence of renal infection. Migraine was treated with sumatriptan after Maxalt was unavailable. Her pancytopenia, including leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, remained stable and consistent with prior trends. Depression and GERD were managed with continued medications. She gradually improved, advanced to oral intake, and was discharged home with TPN, a PICC line, and plans for outpatient follow-up with nutrition support and primary care.
